questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Conjunct and disjunct motion
questions.learningObjective: Identify conjunct motion in a melodic line
questions.stem: In a nurse handover note, a melody moves by step from C to D to E; this motion is best called conjunct.

options.text: Conjunct motion, because every interval is a step of one scale degree
Disjunct motion, because the line changes pitch on each note
options.misconception: confuses any pitch change with a leap

options.text: Static motion, because the notes share the same letter name
options.misconception: misreads stepwise motion as repeated pitch

options.text: Chromatic motion, because the intervals are all semitones
options.misconception: assumes conjunct motion must be chromatic

questions.explanation: Conjunct motion proceeds by steps of one scale degree, so a C-D-E line is conjunct. The tempting idea that any pitch change is a leap is wrong.
questions.hint: Check whether each interval is a step or a leap.

options.text: Three scale degrees using only the interior notes
options.misconception: counts only the notes between the endpoints

questions.explanation: From C to G inclusive spans five scale degrees. Excluding endpoints or mixing chromatic steps gives a wrong count.
questions.hint: Count the starting and ending degrees too.
